problem: Language-based segmentation models (e.g., LAVT) often mask irrelevant regions when the instruction contains multiple referring expressions. They must pick the target phrase among several and output pixel-wise masks, not boxes.
motivation: Domestic service robots need pixel-accurate masks of the object named in a manipulation instruction, and REVERIE-style instructions contain several referring expressions. No existing dataset pairs such instructions with real indoor images and pixel masks. The authors build one and propose a two-stage coarse-to-refine model.
key_idea: Generate a coarse mask with a parallel CLIP+Swin crossmodal encoder and PWAM, then refine it in a second stage with a DDPM-based Crossmodal Reverse Decoder that predicts a residual correction to the mask probability.
insight: Both the parallel CLIP+Swin feature extraction and the diffusion refinement contribute: without diffusion mIoU is 30.19 versus 34.40 with it, and LAVT gets 24.27. The ablation on which intermediate features feed the decoder shows the fine-grained H_it^(0) matters most (dropping it lowers mIoU by 0.65 to 1.55 points). Error analysis shows reference/exophora resolution is the main bottleneck.
method: Crossmodal parallel feature extraction: the image goes in parallel through Swin-B and the CLIP image encoder; the CLIP feature is reshaped, concatenated with the Swin feature on the channel axis, and passed through a 3x3 conv to give V_1.
Language encoding: BERT-base embeds the instruction into H_l.
PWAM (from LAVT) + gated fusion: pixel-word attention fuses V_i with H_l to give F_i. E_i = F_i ⊙ tanh(Conv(F_i)) + V_i feeds the next encoder stage.
Intermediate-step output: multi-scale F_i are decoded by upsampling and concatenation into a softmax mask probability p(y_it), binarized at 0.5. Trained with cross-entropy.
Forward Encoder: standard DDPM forward noising of the image x_0 to x_t.

Crossmodal Reverse Decoder: a pre-trained DDPM UNet predicts noise, and per-layer features are added to H_it^(n_b), resized, and concatenated. An FC+ReLU+BN head predicts Δp, giving p(y_diff) = p(y_it) + Δp. Trained with MAE loss.
SHIMRIE dataset: masks derived from Matterport3D voxel-wise class labels projected with REVERIE camera parameters and bounding boxes, giving 4341 images and 11371 instructions.

setting.backbone: Swin-B + CLIP image encoder + BERT-base + PWAM (trained), plus pre-trained DDPM UNet for the diffusion step
setting.training_data: SHIMRIE (built from REVERIE + Matterport3D): 10153 training samples for the intermediate step; the validation set (856 samples) is used to train the diffusion step
setting.observation: single RGB image (resized to 256x256) + text instruction

numbers.method: Ours (MDSM, with diffusion step and ME)
numbers.extra: mean ± std over 5 runs; test set contains only unseen environments; diffusion step trained on the validation set

numbers_note: Text calls the diffusion variant method (iii) and says removing parallel feature extraction costs 5.92 mIoU, but the table labels the rows differently. SHIMRIE is a new dataset, so there is no standard benchmark. LAVT baseline mIoU is 24.27 (not counted as own).
results: MDSM reaches 34.40 mIoU on SHIMRIE test, +10.13 over LAVT (24.27), and the difference is statistically significant (p<0.05). The parallel CLIP+Swin encoder alone gives +5.92 mIoU, and the diffusion refinement adds a further +4.21.
limitations: Evaluated only on the authors' small SHIMRIE dataset (362 test samples) against a single baseline (LAVT), with low absolute mIoU (~34%) and near-zero P@0.9
Reference/exophora resolution is the main error source; targets outside the image (e.g., the landmark object out of view) cause failures
Not deployed on a physical robot; the diffusion step adds inference cost (0.36 s vs 0.039 s per sample)
